A1.justification: Both ten-page PDFs describe the same VP-CMJL work, with readable and directly matchable text, equations, tables and figures. Both end with references; neither includes the appendix or supplementary material mentioned in the text. The comparison covers all supplied content.

before.justification: v2 reports original VP-CMJL results on four CZSL benchmarks, component ablations in Tables 3–4, and qualitative examples in Figure 4.

after.justification: v4 retains the original benchmark results, ablations and qualitative examples, which continue to qualify as original empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.4 retain the same CLIP/adapters framework, text-guided visual proxies, attention and MLP decoupling, KL alignment, losses and fused inference. Figure 2's revised training/inference labels describe procedures already present in v2.

E1.justification: Both evaluate closed- and open-world CZSL on C-GQA, UT-Zappos and MIT-States, plus closed-world VAW-CZSL. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds IMAX as a comparator under both closed- and open-world settings on all three retained benchmarks. All previous comparator memberships in Tables 1–2 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The documented settings retain CLIP ViT-L/14, 20 training epochs, the same closed/open-world prediction spaces, and S, U, HM and AUC metrics. No revised evaluation procedure or separate protocol for the added IMAX entries is reported.

E4.justification: Tables 3–4 retain the same training/inference component-removal and attention-versus-MLP ablations. Figures 4–5 retain the same qualitative cases and feature-space analysis; their repositioning adds no analysis.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or statistical significance tests. Uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Two IMAX rows add results, while all 37 pre-existing numerical table rows remain identical. For C-GQA closed-world HM/AUC, the strongest baseline changes from Troika's 29.4/12.4 to IMAX's 29.8/12.8; VP-CMJL remains at 34.9/16.3. The qualitative findings are retained.

T1.justification: The modality-space argument, orthogonality condition and Equations 1–23 are unchanged. Section 3.1 repairs training-set notation without changing its membership conditions; no formal assumption, derivation or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about modality alignment, fine-grained discrimination, compositional generalization and benchmark performance. Condensing the abstract does not change their scientific scope.

C2.justification: The explanations of complementary prototype/proxy learning, MIT-States label noise and pruning, and semantic ambiguity in failure cases remain unchanged. No new limitation or applicability boundary is stated.

D1.justification: v4 adds a GitHub location for a future code release in the abstract, absent from v2. The wording promises availability rather than documenting a completed release. The disclosed implementation, initialization and hardware details otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 newly cites the IMAX paper and removes the Masked Channel Modeling citation. The related-work categories, discussion of visual-center learning and novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 condenses the abstract, corrects result cross-references and training-set notation, revises author information, and adds acknowledgements. Section order and most explanatory prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains IMAX rows and is resized; Table 3 and Figures 3 and 5 are repositioned, Figure 4 is enlarged, and Figure 2's labels are revised. The same four tables and five figures remain, with limited caption and layout edits.

improvement.justification: The added IMAX comparison modestly strengthens the empirical context, while corrected cross-references and a shorter abstract improve readability. These gains are partly offset by unreconciled comparisons: Section 4.2 retains C-GQA margins of 5.5/3.9 points although Table 1 now implies 5.1/3.5, and MIT-States unseen-accuracy bolding still highlights Troika's 53.0 instead of IMAX's 53.8. The code-release location is useful information, but availability is only promised.
